origin.description: Concatenate two character vectors with an empty separator.

arguments.name: e1
arguments.text: A character vector or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: e2
arguments.text: A character vector or an object coerced to character.

origin.details: The operator joins two strings the way stri_join does with an empty separator. A missing string stays missing.
origin.example: cat(paste0("c(\"a\", NA) %s+% c(\"b\", \"c\") returns ", paste(ifelse(is.na(c("a", NA) %s+% c("b", "c")), "NA", c("a", NA) %s+% c("b", "c")), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Concatenate two character vectors with an empty separator.

arguments.name: e1
arguments.text: A string, NA, a number, or a list of those.

arguments.name: e2
arguments.text: A string, NA, a number, or a list of those.

translation.details: s_plus calls stri_join(e1, e2, sep=''). It does not reimplement joining. A missing string stays NA, and the string "NA" is text.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing element is NA. None as a whole argument yields an empty list.
translation.example:
shown = ", ".join("NA" if item is NA else item for item in s_plus(["a", NA], ["b", "c"]))
print(f"s_plus(['a', NA], ['b', 'c']) returns {shown}.")
